messages:
maria: Heads up — spotted weird hangs when using Generator.Stream directly in an HTTP handler. Happens under auth token rotation stress on CI.

maria: Short repro: run the Go sample app, hit `/stream` with wrk -c10 -d20s while rotating tokens every 2s. Occasionally the handler never returns and goroutines pile up.

dan: Can you paste the handler? Curious whether stream handshake is using r.Context().

maria: Yep, minimal handler below:
func StreamHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  ctx := r.Context()
  gen := client.Generator("small")
  stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, prompt)
  if err != nil { http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500); return }
  defer stream.Close()
  for ch := range stream.Chunks() { fmt.Fprint(w, ch.Text) }
}

lee: I think the handshake uses the same ctx as the whole stream. If token refresh blocks, the handshake can hang while the HTTP handler is waiting on writes. Close waits for handshake to finish which makes `defer stream.Close()` ineffective in some races.

dan: Short-term workaround: perform handshake on a separate non-cancelable context or with a short timeout so request cancellations don't deadlock handshake: `hsCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)` then `gen.Stream(hsCtx, ...)`.

maria: Tried that — reduces frequency, but we still hit leaks when refresh fails mid-stream.

ci-bot: CI test generator/stream-onboard-flaky: FAIL (timeout) — reproduces with maria's wrk pattern (run 7).

lee: Proposal for SDK: 1) separate handshake context parameter (or `StartStream(ctx, hsCtx, opts)`), 2) make Stream.Close() force-cancel internal goroutines even if handshake pending, 3) document recommended HTTP pattern.

dan: I can draft a small API PR and add a test that rotates tokens under load.

maria: Thanks — I'll open the GH issue with the wrk script and auth-proxy. If anyone else hits this, share OS, go version, and SDK version.
